newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell 28 pct of Mykolayiv alumina plant.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell 28 pct of Mykolayiv alumina plant.

text.p: Ukraine's government plans to sell a 28 percent stake in the Mykolayiv alumina plant (MHZ) to local and foreign strategic investors, a senior MHZ official said on Monday.
MHZ commercial director Valery Agafonov said the government was also likely to transfer its residual 25.1 percent stake in MHZ to the management of the company's managers, but would retain ownership.

"We have positively evaluated the government's privatisation plan and we hope that it will fulfil the president's promises to pass the government's stake to the plant managers," Agafonov told Reuters by telephone from Mykolayiv.

According to the privatisation plan 25.1 percent of the sole Ukrainian alumina plant Mykolayivsky Hlynozemny Zavod would remain in government hands and earlier president Leonid Kuchma had promised to transfer this stake to the plant's authorities.
The government plan also envisages selling 9.62 percent to Ukrainian citizens for privatisation csertificates and 37.28 percent stake will be sold to the plant's workers and managers.
No date for the tender has yet been set.
MHZ's authorised capital is 378.2 million hryvnias.
Agafonov said the plant, built in 1979, produced 960,000 tonnes of alumina last year compared to 996,000 tonnes in 1995.
The plant produces almost all Ukraine's alumina and has traditionally suplied 90 percent of its output to Russia.
Since early 1997 major Russian aluminium smelters have refused to buy alumina from MHZ, saying Ukraine was charging too much.
Agafonov denied Mykolayiv was charging above world prices and added the plant was eager to resolve this problem.

"The Russian market needs our alumina and now we can see the Russian smelters would lose without it," Agafonov said. He added the plant was looking into further cooperation and negotiations with Russian smelters.
The industry ministry said previously that Mykolayiv alumina plant sold 235,000 tonnes of alumina to Tajikistan's sole aluminium smelter Tursuzade in the first three months of this year.
The Mykolayiv plant receives most of its bauxite from the West African country of Guinea.
